subject: Cox regression with piecewise constant baseline hazard fails

messages.author: e656a0f474173df6
messages.subject: Cox regression with piecewise constant baseline hazard fails
parts:
Hi guys,

when I execute the following code 

library(INLA)
library(flexsurv)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
df <- as.tibble(flexsurv::bc)
df <- dplyr::mutate(df, medium=as.integer(group =="Medium"), poor=as.integer(group == "Poor"))
inlaform <- inla.surv(rectime, censrec) ~ medium + poor 
fit <- inla(inlaform, family="coxph", data=df, control.hazard = list(model="rw1", n.intervals=20),
            control.compute = list(dic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

I get the following error

GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>. 

Any ideas how to solve this? I basically apply the example of chapter 6.2.1 of the BRINLA book by Wang, Due and Farraway, just with a different dataset.

parts:
Hi

it works without any problems for me. try to upgrade to the most recent
testing version

inla.upgrade(testing=T)


let me know if that does not work out

H

I use RStudio, but on Linux.
The fact that our plain R had a different INLA indicates that either you have two R installations (one for RStudio and another separate one) or that the package installation paths are setup differently. I don’t see why that would have the effect seen though, as they should be internally consistent.
Make sure to start RStudio cleanly, I.e. without it loading any previous workspace file.

Finn

messages.author: e656a0f474173df6
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Cox regression with piecewise constant baseline hazard fails
parts: Why would you do that, instead of omitting the intercept term and getting rid of the sum-to-zero constraint? Is this documented somewhere in the literature?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Cox regression with piecewise constant baseline hazard fails
parts:
On Wed, 2018-06-06 at 01:07 -0700, Eren Metin Elçi wrote:
> Why would you do that, instead of omitting the intercept term and
> getting rid of the sum-to-zero constraint? Is this documented
> somewhere in the literature?
>

most people would just do

inla.surv(..) ~ ... + x + y + ..

and without the constraint in the baseline hazard, there is a
singularity in the model, then they do not understand why.

there is not much to document, as the two formulations, without
intercept and constr, and with intercept and constr, are eqv.

this is the case where INLA will run slower, as the dimension of the
data and the latent model (beyond the linear predictor) is so large.

to reduce the memory, the most efficient is to reduce the number of
threads.
